summary.text: John Liu is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Senate District 16 in northeast Queens. A former actuary, New York City Councilmember and New York City Comptroller, he has served in the State Senate since 2019 and chairs the New York City Education Committee. He is unopposed in the general election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Taiwan in 1967 and immigrated to the United States at age five; lives in Flushing.
Attended Hunter College High School and Bronx High School of Science, then earned a degree in mathematical physics from Binghamton University.
Worked 14 years in the private sector as an actuary, most recently as a manager at PricewaterhouseCoopers.
Served on the New York City Council representing Flushing and northeast Queens from 2002 to 2009, then as the 43rd New York City Comptroller from 2010 to 2013.
Ran for mayor of New York City in 2013, finishing fourth in the Democratic primary, and lost the 2014 Democratic primary for State Senate District 11 to incumbent Tony Avella.
Defeated Avella in the September 2018 Democratic primary and won the November 2018 general election for State Senate District 11, taking office in January 2019.

Redistricted to District 16 in 2023, succeeding Toby Ann Stavisky; chairs the Senate's New York City Education Committee and is a member of the Education, Finance, Higher Education, Judiciary, Rules and Transportation committees.
Teaches municipal finance and public policy in a graduate program at Columbia University and previously taught at the City University of New York.
